newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on late buying.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on late buying.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates reversed early pressures to close down 60 basis points at 18.65 percent due to late buying by brokers holding hefty liquidity positions, analysts and traders said.

"There was speculative pressure, rates climbed high, but paper came under demand because those who had cash and had been hanging on to it to force rates up stepped in to buy," a fixed-income analyst said.
Overnight Cetes traded as high as at 20.50 percent on liquidity pressures from banks needing to pay balances outstanding on checking accounts held with the central bank.
Another trader said no domestic or international news governed dealing during the day, which was rather driven by the central bank's cutoff date for settling outstanding balances.

Dealers thus forecast paper could be in supply and ease rates down further on Thursday, providing U.S. consumer prices data did not augur interest rate rises at the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Banco de Mexico offset liquidity shortages in the market by injecting 187 million pesos through one credit auction, whic it assigned overnight at 21.58 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed down 110 basis points at 19.50 percent.
June contracts on Cetes futures, meanwhile, gained 10 centavos to 78.60 pesos in trading on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Liquidity of 1.879 billion pesos was due to return to the system on Thursday from prior central bank intervention.
